Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant transition you're going through as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and coping during this postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource for us to assess your emotional well-being after giving birth.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself openly. I want you to feel comfortable sharing your thoughts and feelings with me, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional state over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

Let's get started. I'd like to begin with the first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. to be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it just feels like everything is so overwhelming. I do still enjoy some things, like watching my baby smile or playing with her, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and I don't really feel like laughing or joking around like I used to. Sometimes I'll see something funny, but it's just not as funny to me as it would have been before having the baby. I guess I would say that I've been able to laugh a little bit, but it's just not as often as it used to be, and it doesn't feel as genuine. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I think that's a bit of an understatement for me, to be honest. Like I said, I do still find some things enjoyable, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm only laughing or finding the humor in things maybe...I don't know, once or twice a week? And even then, it's not like I'm really feeling it deeply. It's more like I'm just trying to put on a happy face for my baby or my partner. Most of the time, I just feel really tired and overwhelmed, and it's hard for me to see the funny side of things when I'm feeling that way. I guess I would say that I've been able to laugh a little bit, but it's definitely not as often as it used to be, and it doesn't feel as natural or effortless as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Honestly, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with a friend, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but when the time comes, I just feel so tired and anxious that I don't really enjoy it as much as I thought I would. And sometimes, I'll even find myself feeling really overwhelmed by the thought of doing something, like taking the baby out in public or having people over, and I'll just end up feeling really anxious and stuck. I used to love trying new things and going out with friends, but now it all just feels like so much work. I do still look forward to some quiet time with my baby, like when we're just sitting together and she's sleeping, but even that can be stressful sometimes because I worry about her waking up and needing something. I guess I would say that I don't really feel like I'm looking forward to things with enjoyment like I used to. It's all just feeling really hard and overwhelming right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I'd say that's definitely been happening to me. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already so hard on myself, and when things go wrong, it's easy for me to fall into the trap of thinking that it's all my fault. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "I'm a terrible mother, I should be able to figure this out." Or, if I'm feeling really overwhelmed and I need to ask for help, I'll think, "I'm not doing this right, I'm not cut out for this." It's like, I know logically that I'm doing the best I can, but it's hard for me to shake the feeling that I'm just not good enough. And it's not just the big things, either - it's the little things, like if I forget to do something or if I make a mistake with the baby's schedule. I'll beat myself up over it and think that I'm just not capable of being a good mom. It's really hard for me to be kind to myself and remind myself that it's okay to make mistakes. Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing everything wrong and that I'm not fit to be a mother. It's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

.. this is something that's been really getting to me lately. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the house catches on fire or what if someone breaks in. Or I'll worry about the baby's health, like what if she's not gaining enough weight or what if she's got some kind of underlying condition that we don't know about. It's like, I know these are irrational thoughts, but I just can't seem to shake them. And it's not just the big things, either - I'll worry about little things, like what if I forget to buy diapers or what if I run out of formula. It's like, my mind is just constantly racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and it's exhausting. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start worrying about everything, and I won't be able to fall asleep. It's like, I know I need to calm down and focus on the present moment, but it's hard for me to do that when my mind is just racing with all these anxious thoughts. I feel like I'm just constantly on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. It's really hard to deal with, and it's affecting my ability to enjoy time with my baby and my partner.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... this has been happening to me a lot lately. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, I know there's no reason to be scared, but I just can't help how I'm feeling. Sometimes it's triggered by something, like a loud noise or a sudden movement, but other times it just comes out of nowhere. I'll be feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll feel like I'm going to drop her or that something terrible is going to happen to her. Or I'll be walking down the street, and I'll feel like I'm going to get hurt or that someone is following me. It's like, I know it's irrational, but it's hard to shake the feeling of fear. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - sometimes I'll be with my partner or friends, and I'll still feel this sense of panic. It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always on edge, just waiting for the other shoe to drop. And it's hard to explain to my partner or friends, because they just tell me to "calm down" or "relax," but it's not that easy. I feel like I'm losing control, and it's really scary. Sometimes I just feel like I'm going to break down or something, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's a huge understatement. I feel like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it all just feels so overwhelming. And it's not just the big things, either - it's the little things, like laundry and dishes and meal planning, that just feel like they're suffocating me. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. Some days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together, and that if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart. I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, trying to get everything done, but it's just not possible. And then I feel guilty, because I feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not doing it well enough. It's like, I know I'm trying my best, but it just doesn't feel like it's good enough. And that feeling of inadequacy is just weighing on me, making it even harder to cope with everything else. Sometimes I just feel like I'm at my breaking point, and I don't know how much more I can handle.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because my mind is just racing all the time. I'll lie in bed, and I'll just start thinking about everything that's going wrong, or everything that I need to do, or everything that I'm worried about. And I just can't seem to turn it off. I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, feeling anxious and overwhelmed. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so unsettling. Sometimes I'll wake up feeling more tired than when I went to bed, which just makes everything worse. I've been trying to establish a bedtime routine, but it's hard when my mind is just racing all the time. I've been having trouble falling asleep, and then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just lie there, feeling anxious and worried. It's like, I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but I just can't seem to get it. And that just adds to my feelings of guilt and inadequacy, which makes it even harder to sleep. It's just this vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break it. Some nights, I'll be up for hours, just feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed, and I'll just cry, because I don't know what else to do.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really feeling any joy or happiness. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll think, "I should be feeling so happy and grateful right now," but instead, I just feel empty and sad. It's like, I know I love my baby, but I just can't seem to shake this feeling of misery. Sometimes it's overwhelming, and I'll just break down in tears for no reason. Other times, it's just a dull, constant feeling of sadness that I just can't seem to escape. I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, like I'm just disappearing into motherhood and I don't know who I am anymore. It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'm just feeling so much pain and sadness, and I don't know how to make it stop. I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but I don't think they really understand. They just tell me to "be happy" and "enjoy this time," but it's not that easy. I feel like I'm just pretending to be a happy mom, but inside, I'm dying. It's a really hard feeling to deal with, and it's making it hard for me to bond with my baby, which just makes me feel even more guilty and sad.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. It can be triggered by anything - a commercial on TV, a song on the radio, a conversation with my partner... or it can just come out of nowhere. I'll be feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm feeling overwhelmed. Or I'll be changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm feeling so frustrated. It's like, I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to control it. Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just sitting there, feeling so sad and miserable. And it's not just the big things that make me cry - it's the little things, too. Like, I'll cry because I'm feeling so tired, or because I'm feeling so guilty for not being a better mom. I feel like I'm just losing control, and it's really scary. My partner will try to comfort me, but sometimes I just push them away because I don't know how to explain how I'm feeling. I feel like I'm just a mess, and I don't know how to clean myself up. The crying is just a release, I guess, but it's also really exhausting. I feel like I'm just crying all the time, and it's taking a toll on my relationships and my daily life. I just wish I could stop crying and feel happy again, but I don't know how to make that happen.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

.. (pausing, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yes... I have to admit, there have been times when I've thought about harming myself. It's like, the feelings of sadness and hopelessness just get so overwhelming, and I don't know how to make them stop. I feel like I'm drowning in my own emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. Sometimes, when I'm feeling really desperate, I'll think about just... escaping, I guess. Not really thinking about how or why, just that I want the pain to stop. It's not something I've ever acted on, and it's not something I think I would ever do, but... (pausing, struggling to hold back tears) it's just that the thoughts are there, and they scare me. I don't know how to make them go away. I feel like I'm a terrible person for even thinking about it, like I'm a failure as a mom and a person. (starting to cry) I just wish I could feel happy again, and that these thoughts would just go away. I don't know how to deal with them, and it's really frightening. ( sobbing )

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns following the birth of their baby, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure in activities, and frequent crying spells. They report difficulty coping with daily responsibilities, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, and significant anxiety. The patient's safety is a concern due to thoughts of self-harm.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient mentions they can only laugh or find humor in things once or twice a week and it doesn't feel deep or natural, indicating a significant decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things.</sym>, <sym>Definitely less than I used to'.</sym>, <sym>The patient explicitly states that self-blame has 'definitely been happening' to them and provides multiple examples of situations where they blame themselves, indicating a frequent occurrence of self-blame.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety, describing themselves as 'always on edge' and experiencing constant worried thoughts, even about irrational things, which aligns with 'Yes, very often'.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports feeling scared or panicky frequently, with intense physical symptoms and a pervasive sense of fear, even in everyday situations, matching the 'Yes, quite a lot' option.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been experiencing difficulty sleeping due to unhappiness most of the time, as evidenced by statements such as 'that's been me lately' and 'I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports crying frequently, often without a specific trigger, and describes feeling overwhelmed, frustrated, and sad, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to having thoughts of self-harm, describing them as occurring when feelings of sadness and hopelessness become overwhelming, but states these thoughts are not something they've acted on and don't think they would, matching the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med> and anxiety. Their symptoms, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and thoughts of self-harm, are consistent with <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med> as described in the <med>DSM-5</med>. The patient's difficulty sleeping, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, and significant anxiety also support this screening impression. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if thoughts of self-harm persist
3. Support patient in establishing a daily routine and coping mechanisms for anxiety and stress
4. Recommend sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
5. Educate patient on <med>postpartum depression</med> and anxiety, and the importance of seeking professional help
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
